title: Console: surface Dedicated tier + throughput status (vs guarantee) with docs/exports links
creator: Lauren Bishop
description:
## Context
Dedicated customers (and internal teams) need a simple, customer-facing way to confirm:
1) what Dedicated tier they’re on (Standard / Performance / Premium),
2) what their current throughput is vs the tier guarantee (per measurement standard),
3) whether they are being throttled due to tier limits / overload protection,
4) where to find the authoritative definitions (SLO + measurement standard) and how to export the underlying metrics.

This is explicitly **minimal UI** to support the Dedicated throughput tier launch; not a full console redesign.

## Problem
Today, Dedicated console pages don’t clearly communicate tier entitlements or how throughput is measured. When a customer feels “slow”, they often conflate latency with throughput or don’t understand what is guaranteed (and under what assumptions). Support ends up routing people to internal dashboards.

## Goals
- Provide a clear, low-ambiguity “Throughput status” section per Dedicated deployment.
- Reduce Support/CS time-to-triage for “throughput below expectation” tickets.
- Align UI language with the formal SLO definition and measurement standard.

## Non-goals
- Building a bespoke customer dashboard builder.
- Adding customer-editable tier policy controls (admission control knobs remain internal for beta).
- Replacing Grafana for internal oncall.

## Proposed UI surface (v1)
### Placement
Dedicated deployment details page (Console → Dedicated → Deployment → Overview).

### Components
1) **Tier badge + entitlement summary**
   - Show: Tier name (Standard/Performance/Premium)
   - Show: Hardware shape (if available in console today) as secondary text (e.g., “H100 x 1”, “A100 80GB x 2”) with tooltip: “Shape impacts baseline throughput; guarantee is defined by tier and measurement standard.”

2) **Throughput status card**
   - Primary metric: “Sustained output throughput” (units: tokens/sec)
   - Display: Current (or last 5 minutes) measured throughput vs guarantee for the tier
   - Suggested format:
     - Big number: “X tok/s”
     - Secondary: “Guarantee: ≥ Y tok/s (sustained, 5m window)”
     - Status pill: “Meeting guarantee” / “At risk” / “Below guarantee”

3) **Measurement context + caveats (collapsed by default)**
   - Short text: “Measured as sustained output tokens/sec over a rolling window. Excludes maintenance windows and customer-induced errors.”
   - Expand/collapse section with 3–5 bullet caveats only (avoid dumping full spec).
   - Link to: “Read full throughput measurement standard”

4) **Throttling / overload visibility**
   - Show an info row when throttling is non-zero:
     - “Throttling active: Z% of requests rate-limited in last 5m”
     - Link: “Learn about overload protection” (doc)
   - If we have a specific reason code from gateway/admission control, show it in tooltip (e.g., burst limit exceeded, queue depth cap).

5) **Exports / diagnostics**
   - Provide two actions:
     - “Download CSV (last 24h)” for throughput + throttling rate (customer safe)
     - “Copy metrics query” (optional; might be internal-only during beta)
   - Also link to “How to share telemetry with Support” (Support template)

## Data requirements (design assumptions)
Design should assume the backend will provide:
- Tier string: {standard|performance|premium}
- Windowed throughput number: throughput_tok_s (rolling 5m) and guarantee_tok_s (tier)
- Status classification computed server-side OR client-side with clear thresholds
- Throttling rate: throttled_requests_rate (rolling 5m) and/or throttled_requests_pct
- Timestamp for last data point + data freshness indicator

## States / edge cases
- **No data yet**: brand new deployment; show skeleton + “Collecting baseline metrics (up to ~10 minutes)”
- **Data stale**: show warning: “Metrics delayed” with tooltip (do not imply SLO breach)
- **Below guarantee but throttling > 0**: copy should clarify: “Throughput limited by tier policy (throttling).” This should *not* read as Redwood missing the guarantee.
- **Below guarantee and throttling == 0**: show “Below guarantee” + CTA “Contact Support” + link to export.
- **During maintenance window**: avoid red status; show neutral state “Maintenance in progress” (if control plane can expose).
- **Multiple models**: if the deployment runs multiple models/routes, initial v1 can scope to “Deployment aggregate” with a link: “View per-model breakdown (coming soon)” unless per-model is already supported by dashboards.

## Copy guidelines (must match SLO semantics)
- Avoid “SLA” language in console unless Legal signs off; use “SLO” / “guarantee” per PM guidance.
- Prefer “tokens/sec (output)” instead of generic “throughput” wherever space allows.
- Make throttling explicit and non-alarming when it is expected behavior.

## Acceptance criteria
- Dedicated deployment details page shows tier badge and throughput status card.
- Card displays current throughput, guarantee value, and status.
- Customer can access:
  - Link to SLO definition page
  - Link to measurement standard page
  - CSV export for last 24h (or a clearly labeled beta alternative)
- Copy includes a short caveats section aligned with measurement standard.
- Includes empty/loading/stale states with non-misleading messaging.

## Deliverables
- Figma frame(s) for:
  - Overview page section (default)
  - Empty/loading/stale
  - Throttling active
  - Below guarantee (no throttling)
- Interaction notes + redlines
- Copy doc snippet to share with PM/Legal/SRE

## Open questions
1) Source of truth for guarantee value: is it tier-only or tier+shape+region?
2) Do we surface p50 vs p95 throughput or only a single sustained value?
3) Should “Copy metrics query” be internal-only for beta?
4) Do we expose a customer-visible “SLO compliance (last 30d)” summary or defer to later?

## Links
- PM PRD: PM-482
- Dashboards/alerts work: ENG-2201
- Metrics instrumentation: ENG-2194
- Project docs: Dedicated throughput SLO + tier definitions (Confluence) (pending final link)
comments: 2025-02-06 (Chloe Martin): Drafted initial component layout for Deployment Overview. Keeping scope tight: tier badge + single throughput card + export link. Need confirmation on which window (5m vs 15m) we want visible by default.

2025-02-07 (Lauren Bishop): For UI, default to 5m rolling window and label it explicitly. Also please avoid “SLA” wording; Legal wants console to say “SLO” + link to contract language lives elsewhere.

2025-02-10 (Sergio Costa): From dashboard spec we’ll have rolling 5m throughput and throttling rate. Per-model breakdown is heavy; recommend we keep v1 deployment aggregate to avoid cardinality surprises.

2025-02-12 (Aisha Bello): Important nuance: throttling is expected behavior when customers exceed tier burst policy. UI should not show “Below guarantee” in red if throttling is the reason; that’s “limited by policy” not an SLO miss.

2025-02-14 (Chloe Martin): Updated designs to include 3-state status: Meeting / At risk / Below. Added separate banner when throttling > 0: “Overload protection active” with tooltip explaining expected behavior and how to request capacity change.
2025-02-18 (Rafael Mendes): Add a “data freshness” indicator. During metrics pipeline delay we don’t want false escalations. Even a small “Updated 2m ago” line helps Support.

2025-02-20 (Lauren Bishop): Re: guarantee value, tier-only for now. If we later introduce shape-specific guarantees, we’ll revisit. Also want a CSV export link even if it’s a simple pre-baked endpoint; Support asked for it explicitly.
2025-02-26 (Chloe Martin): Finalizing copy + redlines for handoff. Next step: coordinate with ENG-2201 on which exact fields are available in the API response to avoid last-minute UI rework.
